govdocs-archive_org-nsia-WBBM_WBBM: A viewer wrote to Mr. Madigan on May 10, 1970, about a WBBM-TV program on the Kennedy assassination. The letter criticizes the station for treating the killing in a frivolous way. Complaints like this one reached many stations that aired assassination programs in those years. The letter preserves an ordinary viewer's anger at how television handled a national wound.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-WCBM_WCBM: Harold Weisberg wrote to Mr. Dougherty of Metromedia and WCBM on January 29, 1968, about a broadcast. Weisberg watched radio and television coverage of the Kennedy assassination closely and wrote often when he thought it wrong. The letter belongs to his long paper campaign against the Warren Commission's defenders in the media. It shows a researcher treating broadcasters as people who had to answer for their programs.
podcast-joerogan-gF0CrAx_sBM:
Filmmaker Ky Dickens joins the Joe Rogan Experience for episode 2279. Dickens directs documentaries that chase big questions, including a well-known film series on telepathy and minds that work in ways science struggles to explain. Rogan's studio is a natural home for her subjects.

She talks about the films she has made and the stories she hunts, and what years behind the camera taught her about witnesses. Rogan asks how a filmmaker grades a claim she cannot film. The episode is a behind-the-lens talk with a documentarian whose work lives on the border between evidence and wonder.
podcast-tuckercarlson-KMsklsr_nBM:
Blackouts and water shortages loom in this Tucker Carlson episode warning about the AI build-out. Carlson argues that tech giants are racing to build vast data centers that strain power grids and water supplies. He says anyone who resists the crush gets pushed aside.

The episode lays out how much energy and water the new AI centers demand. Carlson questions why local towns should bear the costs for distant companies' profits. He frames the boom as a dystopia built in plain sight. Wary viewers get a dark forecast of the machine age and a call to slow it down.
